This would be an ok place if it were used appropriately: posts in the vein of 'I'm 12 and what's this?' and 'I can't figure this out, halp plz' are fine. The problem is the overflow of blogposts and testimonials - there's nothing wrong with them or the authors as such, those posts would be ok in /jumpedship, /exodus or /asl or as individual profile information, but this really shouldn't be the place from them.

As new users are guided here, this is going to be one of the first and most imporatnt places for them to absorb the etiquette and the culture of the whole site. Yet, this place is set up in a very 'safe place-ish' way that almost any behavior is reinforced because users here are after accuring points instead any quality posts or discussion of any kind. There's not much anyone can do to discourage this behavior either as it stands at the moment, well, short of going to the thread and voicing negative opinions about the original post which could be considered to be against the courteousness rule. Someone blogging about their life will take the lack of negative votes to mean that this is an acceptable behavior for the site and will take this with them to other subforums which will only cause strife and misunderstanding later. Or turn a subforum into a personal blogging platform instead of a a place of discussion and debate. Most other users here, being new, can't really do anything to discourage it since negative votes require work. If this place didn't exist new users would have to get their first impressions at individual subforums which would enable those communities to develop their own distict culture and discourage irrelevant and detrimental information being posted.

This place here means that someone who joins the site, gets a positive reinforcement here and then starts seeking out subforums to join instead of joining a subforum and getting reinforced because they joined one most suited for them. In the latter case if the community doesn't react positively to them, then the user will probably seek out another similiar yet more fitting subforum, say going from /comics to /comicbookmovies. In the first case, however, they are already reinforced and vindicated in their own eyes by this hugbox or positiveness-circlejerk here and will see themselves being right with the whole community being wrong.
